All available answers appear to lie along a straight line between their position and yours. Often the only creative thinking shown is to suggest splitting the difference.

拥有多种选择固然重要，但谈判者往往很少意识到这种必要性。在争端中，人们通常认为自己掌握了正确答案——他们的观点应该占上风。在合同谈判中，他们同样倾向于认为自己的报价合理，应该被采纳，或许价格可以稍作调整。所有可行的方案似乎都介于他们的立场和你的立场之间。通常，他们唯一展现出的创造性思维就是提出折中方案。

In most negotiations there are four major obstacles that inhibit the inventing of an abundance of options: (1) premature judgment; (2) searching for the single answer; (3) the assumption of a fixed pie; and (4) thinking that “solving their problem is their problem.” To overcome these constraints, you need to understand them.

大多数谈判中，有四大障碍会阻碍人们提出多种选择：（1）过早下结论；（2）寻求唯一答案；（3）假定蛋糕大小固定不变；（4）认为“解决他们的问题是他们的事”。要克服这些限制，你需要了解它们。

Premature judgment

过早下结论

Inventing options does not come naturally. Not inventing is the normal state of affairs, even when you are outside a stressful negotiation. If you were asked to name the one person in the world most deserving of the Nobel Peace Prize, any answer you might start to propose would immediately encounter your reservations and doubts. How could you be sure that that person was the most deserving? Your mind might well go blank, or you might throw out a few answers that would reflect conventional thinking: “Well, maybe the Pope, or the President.”

创造新的方案并非易事。即便在压力巨大的谈判之外，不去创造方案才是常态。如果有人问你，世界上谁最应该获得诺贝尔和平奖，你提出的任何答案都会立刻遇到你的顾虑和怀疑。你怎么能确定这个人就是最合适的呢？你很可能会大脑一片空白，或者抛出一些符合传统思维的答案：“嗯，也许是教皇，或者总统。”

Nothing is so harmful to inventing as a critical sense waiting to pounce on the drawbacks of any new idea. Judgment hinders imagination.

没有什么比批判意识更能阻碍创新，它总是伺机挑剔任何新想法的缺陷。评判会扼杀想象力。

Under the pressure of a forthcoming negotiation, your critical sense is likely to be sharper. Practical negotiation appears to call for practical thinking, not wild ideas.

在即将到来的谈判压力下，你的批判性思维可能会更加敏锐。务实的谈判似乎需要的是务实的思考，而不是天马行空的想法。

Your creativity may be even more stifled by the presence of those on the other side. Suppose you are negotiating with your boss over your salary for the coming year. You have asked for a $4,000 raise; your boss has offered you $1,500, a figure that you have indicated is unsatisfactory. In a tense situation like this you are not likely to start inventing imaginative solutions. You may fear that if you suggest some bright half-baked idea like taking half the increase in a raise and half in additional benefits, you might look foolish. Your boss might say, “Be serious. You know better than that. It would upset company policy. I am surprised that you even suggested it.” If on the spur of the moment you invent a possible option of spreading out the raise over time, your boss may take it as an offer: “I’m prepared to start negotiating on that basis.” Since whatever you say may be taken as a commitment, you will think twice before saying anything.

对方的存在可能会进一步扼杀你的创造力。假设你正在和老板协商来年的薪水。你要求加薪4000美元；老板只愿意给你1500美元，你表示这个数字并不满意。在这种紧张的情况下，你不太可能想出什么有创意的解决方案。你可能会担心，如果你提出一些看似不错但并不成熟的想法，比如把加薪的一半作为工资，另一半作为额外的福利，会显得很愚蠢。你的老板可能会说：“别开玩笑了。你应该知道这样做不妥。这会违反公司政策。我很惊讶你居然会提出这种建议。” 如果你灵机一动，想出一个分期加薪的方案，你的老板可能会把它当成一个提议：“我愿意以此为基础开始谈判。” 因为你说的任何话都可能被视为承诺，所以你说话之前都会三思而后行。

You may also fear that by inventing options you will disclose some piece of information that will jeopardize your bargaining position. If you should suggest, for example, that the company help finance the house you are about to buy, your boss may conclude that you intend to stay and that you will in the end accept any raise in salary the boss decides to offer.

你可能还会担心，提出一些选项会泄露一些信息，从而损害你的谈判地位。例如，如果你建议公司帮助你贷款购买即将购买的房子，你的老板可能会认为你打算留下来，最终会接受老板提出的任何加薪方案。

Searching for the single answer

寻找唯一答案

In most people’s minds, inventing simply is not part of the negotiating process. People see their job as narrowing the gap between positions, not broadening the options available. They tend to think, “We’re having a hard enough time agreeing as it is. The last thing we need is a bunch of different ideas.” Since the end product of negotiation is a single decision, they fear that free-floating discussion will only delay and confuse the process.

在大多数人看来，创造新方案并非谈判过程的一部分。人们认为自己的职责是缩小立场差距，而不是拓宽选择范围。他们往往会想：“我们本来就很难达成一致，最不需要的就是一堆不同的想法。” 由于谈判的最终结果只有一个决定，他们担心漫无目的的讨论只会拖延和扰乱进程。

If the first impediment to creative thinking is premature criticism, the second is premature closure. By looking from the outset for the single best answer, you are likely to short-circuit a wiser decision-making process in which you select from a large number of possible answers.

如果说阻碍创造性思维的第一大障碍是过早的批评，那么第二大障碍就是过早的下结论。从一开始就寻找唯一最佳答案，很可能会阻碍更明智的决策过程——在这个过程中，你需要从众多可能的答案中进行选择。

The assumption of a fixed pie

假设饼图大小固定不变

A third explanation for why there may be so few good options on the table is that each side sees the situation as essentially either/or—either I get what is in dispute or you do. A negotiation often appears to be a “fixed-sum” game; $100 more for you on the price of a car means $100 less for me. Why bother to invent if all the options are obvious and I can satisfy you only at my own expense?

第三个解释是，为什么摆在桌面上的好选择如此之少，是因为双方都把情况看作非此即彼——要么我得到争议的那部分，要么你得到。谈判往往看起来像是一场“固定和博弈”；你多付100美元买车，我就少付100美元。既然所有选择都显而易见，而我只能自掏腰包才能满足你，那我又何必费心去想办法呢？

Thinking that “solving their problem is their problem”

认为“解决他们的问题是他们自己的问题”

A final obstacle to inventing realistic options lies in each side’s concern with only its own immediate interests. For you as a negotiator to reach an agreement that meets your own self-interest, you need to develop a solution that also appeals to the self-interest of the other. Yet emotional involvement on one side of an issue makes it difficult to achieve the detachment necessary to think up wise ways of meeting the interests of both sides: “We’ve got enough problems of our own; they can look after theirs.” There also frequently exists a psychological reluctance to accord any legitimacy to the views of the other side; it seems disloyal to think up ways to satisfy them. Shortsighted self-concern thus leads a negotiator to develop only partisan positions, partisan arguments, and one-sided solutions.

阻碍制定切实可行方案的最后一个障碍在于，双方都只关注自身的眼前利益。作为谈判者，要想达成符合自身利益的协议，你需要找到一个既能满足对方利益又能兼顾双方利益的方案。然而，一方的情感投入会使人难以保持客观冷静，从而难以找到兼顾双方利益的明智之举：“我们自己的问题已经够多了，让他们自己解决吧。”此外，人们常常在心理上不愿承认对方的观点，认为满足对方的要求是不忠诚的。因此，目光短浅的利己主义会导致谈判者最终只提出带有党派色彩的立场、论点和片面的解决方案。

PRESCRIPTION

处方

To invent creative options, then, you will need to (1) separate the act of inventing options from the act of judging them; (2) broaden the options on the table rather than look for a single answer; (3) search for mutual gains; and (4) invent ways of making their decisions easy. Each of these steps is discussed below.

因此，要想出创造性的方案，你需要做到以下几点：（1）将提出方案和评估方案分开；（2）拓宽选项范围，而不是只寻找单一答案；（3）寻求互惠互利；（4）想办法简化决策过程。以下将逐一讨论这些步骤。

Separate inventing from deciding

将发明与决策分开

Since judgment hinders imagination, separate the creative act from the critical one; separate the process of thinking up possible decisions from the process of selecting among them. Invent first, decide later.

既然判断会阻碍想象力，那就把创造行为与批判行为分开；把构思各种可能决策的过程与从中选择决策的过程分开。先创造，后决策。

As a negotiator, you will of necessity do much inventing by yourself. It is not easy. By definition, inventing new ideas requires you to think about things that are not already in your mind. You should therefore consider the desirability of arranging an inventing or brainstorming session with a few colleagues or friends. Such a session can effectively separate inventing from deciding.

作为谈判者，你必然需要独立进行大量的创新。这并非易事。顾名思义，创新需要你思考那些你原本没有想到的事情。因此，你应该考虑与几位同事或朋友组织一次头脑风暴会议。这样的会议可以有效地将创新与决策分开。

A brainstorming session is designed to produce as many ideas as possible to solve the problem at hand. The key ground rule is to postpone all criticism and evaluation of ideas. The group simply invents ideas without pausing to consider whether they are good or bad, realistic or unrealistic. With those inhibitions removed, one idea should stimulate another, like firecrackers setting off one another.

头脑风暴会议旨在尽可能多地提出解决当前问题的想法。其关键原则是暂缓对任何想法进行批评和评价。团队成员只需自由地提出想法，无需考虑其好坏、现实与否。抛开这些顾虑，一个想法就能激发另一个想法，如同鞭炮互相引爆一般。

In a brainstorming session, people need not fear looking foolish since wild ideas are explicitly encouraged. And in the absence of the other side, negotiators need not worry about disclosing confidential information or having a half-baked idea taken as a serious commitment.

在头脑风暴会议中，人们不必担心显得愚蠢，因为会议明确鼓励提出天马行空的想法。而且，由于对方不在场，谈判者也不必担心泄露机密信息，或者让一个不成熟的想法被当作严肃的承诺。

There is no right way to run a brainstorming session. Rather, you should tailor it to your needs and resources. In doing so, you may find it useful to consider the following guidelines.

头脑风暴会议没有固定的模式。你应该根据自身需求和资源进行调整。在此过程中，以下指导原则或许对你有所帮助。

Before brainstorming:

头脑风暴之前：

1. Define your purpose. Think of what you would like to walk out of the meeting with.

1. 明确你的会议目的。想想你希望通过这次会议获得什么。

2. Choose a few participants. The group should normally be large enough to provide a stimulating interchange, yet small enough to encourage both individual participation and free-wheeling inventing—usually between five and eight people.

2. 选择几名参与者。小组人数通常应足够多，以便进行有益的交流，但又应足够少，以鼓励个人参与和自由发挥——通常在五到八人之间。

3. Change the environment. Select a time and place distinguishing the session as much as possible from regular discussions. The more different a brainstorming session seems from a normal meeting, the easier it is for participants to suspend judgment.

3. 改变环境。选择一个时间和地点，尽可能将头脑风暴会议与日常讨论区分开来。头脑风暴会议与普通会议的差异越大，参与者就越容易放下成见。

4. Design an informal atmosphere. What does it take for you and others to relax? It may be talking over a drink, or meeting at a vacation lodge in some picturesque spot, or dressing less formally during the meeting and calling one another by your first names.

4. 营造轻松的氛围。怎样才能让你和其他人放松下来？也许是边喝饮料边聊天，或者是在风景如画的度假小屋见面，又或者是在会议期间穿着不那么正式，彼此直呼其名。

5. Choose a facilitator. Someone at the meeting needs to facilitate—to keep the meeting on track, to make sure everyone gets a chance to speak, to enforce any ground rules, and to stimulate discussion by asking questions.

5. 选择一位主持人。会议中需要有人担任主持人——确保会议按计划进行，确保每个人都有机会发言，执行各项基本规则，并通过提问来激发讨论。

During brainstorming:

在头脑风暴期间：

1. Seat the participants side by side facing the problem. The physical reinforces the psychological. Physically sitting side by side can reinforce the mental attitude of tackling a common problem together. People facing each other tend to respond personally and engage in dialogue or argument; people sitting side by side in a semicircle of chairs facing a flip chart or whiteboard tend to respond to the problem depicted there.

1. 让参与者并排面向问题而坐。这种物理上的安排能够强化心理上的配合。并排而坐可以强化共同解决问题的心理状态。面对面的人往往会更倾向于个人化地回应，并展开对话或争论；而围坐在半圆形椅子上，面向挂图或白板的人则更倾向于关注上面呈现的问题。

2. Clarify the ground rules, including the no-criticism rule. If the participants do not all know each other, the meeting begins with introductions all around, followed by clarification of the ground rules. Outlaw negative criticism of any kind.

2. 明确会议规则，包括禁止批评的规定。如果参会人员彼此不认识，会议开始时先进行自我介绍，然后明确会议规则。严禁任何形式的负面批评。

Joint inventing produces new ideas because each of us invents only within the limits set by our working assumptions. If ideas are shot down unless they appeal to all participants, the implicit goal becomes to advance an idea that no one will shoot down. If, on the other hand, wild ideas are encouraged, even those that in fact lie well outside the realm of the possible, the group may generate from these ideas other options that are possible and that no one would previously have considered.

共同发明之所以能产生新想法，是因为我们每个人只能在自身工作假设的框架内进行发明创造。如果想法必须得到所有参与者的认可才能被否决，那么其隐含的目标就变成了提出一个无人会否决的想法。相反，如果鼓励天马行空的想法，即使是那些实际上远远超出可能性范围的想法，团队也可能从中衍生出其他可行的方案，而这些方案此前可能从未被考虑过。

Other ground rules you may want to adopt are to make the entire session off the record and to refrain from attributing ideas to any participant.

你可能想要遵循的其他基本规则包括：整个会议内容不予记录，并且不要将任何想法归功于任何参与者。

3. Brainstorm. Once the purpose of the meeting is clear, let your imaginations go. Try to come up with a long list of ideas, approaching the question from every conceivable angle.

3. 集思广益。一旦会议目的明确，就尽情发挥想象力。尝试列出一长串想法，从各个可能的角度来探讨这个问题。

4. Record the ideas in full view. Recording ideas either on a whiteboard or flipcharts gives the group a tangible sense of collective achievement; it reinforces the no-criticism rule; it reduces the tendency to repeat; and it helps stimulate other ideas.

4. 将想法记录在众目睽睽之下。将想法记录在白板或挂图上，能让小组成员切实感受到集体的成就感；强化不批评的原则；减少重复的倾向；并有助于激发其他想法。

After brainstorming:

经过头脑风暴：

1. Star the most promising ideas. After brainstorming, relax the no-criticism rule to begin winnowing out the most promising ideas. You are still not at the stage of deciding; you are merely nominating ideas worth developing further. Mark those ideas that members of the group think are best.

1. 标记最有前景的想法。头脑风暴结束后，放宽“不批评”的规则，开始筛选出最有前景的想法。此时你们还未到最终决定阶段；你们只是在提名值得进一步发展的想法。标记出小组成员认为最好的那些想法。

2. Invent improvements for promising ideas. Take one promising idea and invent ways to make it better and more realistic, as well as ways to carry it out. The task at this stage is to make the idea as attractive as you can. Preface constructive criticism with: “What I like best about that idea is . . . . Might it be even better if . . . ?”

2. 为有前景的想法提出改进方案。选择一个有前景的想法，并思考如何使其更好、更现实，以及如何实施这些改进方案。这个阶段的任务是尽可能地让这个想法更具吸引力。提出建设性批评之前，可以这样开头：“我最喜欢这个想法的地方是……如果……会不会更好？”

3. Set up a time to evaluate ideas and decide. Before you break, draw up a selective and improved list of ideas from the session and set up a time for deciding which of these ideas to advance in your negotiation and how.

3. 安排时间评估想法并做出决定。在休息之前，整理出一份经过筛选和改进的想法清单，并安排时间决定在谈判中推进哪些想法以及如何推进。

Consider brainstorming with the other side. Although more difficult than brainstorming with your own side, brainstorming with people from the other side can also prove extremely valuable. It is more difficult because of the increased risk that you will say something that prejudices your interests despite the rules established for a brainstorming session. You may disclose confidential information inadvertently or lead the other side to mistake an option you devise for an offer. Nevertheless, joint brainstorming sessions have the great advantages of producing ideas that take into account the interests of all those involved, of creating a climate of joint problem-solving, and of educating each side about the concerns of the other.

不妨考虑与对方进行头脑风暴。虽然这比与己方进行头脑风暴更具挑战性，但与对方人员共同头脑风暴也可能极具价值。之所以更具挑战性，是因为即使遵循头脑风暴会议的既定规则，你仍然有可能说出损害自身利益的话。你可能会无意中泄露机密信息，或者让对方误以为你提出的方案是正式的提议。然而，联合头脑风暴会议的优势在于：能够产生兼顾所有参与者利益的想法，营造共同解决问题的氛围，并让双方了解彼此的顾虑。

To protect yourself when brainstorming with the other side, distinguish the brainstorming session explicitly from a negotiating session where people state official views and speak on the record. People are so accustomed to meeting for the purpose of reaching agreement that any other purpose needs to be clearly stated.

为了在与对方进行头脑风暴时保护自己，务必将头脑风暴会议与谈判会议明确区分开来。在谈判会议中，人们会阐述官方观点并公开发言。人们已经习惯于为了达成协议而开会，因此任何其他目的都需要明确说明。

To reduce the risk of appearing committed to any given idea, you can make a habit of advancing at least two alternatives at the same time. You can also put on the table options with which you obviously disagree. “I could give you the house for nothing, or you could pay me a million dollars in cash for it, or . . . .” Since you are plainly not proposing either of these ideas, the ones that follow are labeled as mere possibilities, not proposals.

为了降低给人留下坚持己见的印象，你可以养成同时提出至少两种备选方案的习惯。你也可以提出一些你明显不认同的选项。“我可以免费把房子送给你，或者你可以给我一百万美元现金，或者……”既然你显然没有提出这些方案，那么接下来的选项就只能算是可能性，而非正式提议。

To get the flavor of a joint brainstorming session, let us suppose the leaders of a local union are meeting with the management of a coal mine to brainstorm on ways to reduce unauthorized one- or two-day strikes. Ten people—five from each side—are present, sitting around a table facing a whiteboard. A neutral facilitator asks the participants for their ideas, and writes them up on the whiteboard.

为了体验联合头脑风暴会议的氛围，我们假设当地工会的领导人与煤矿管理层正在开会，商讨如何减少未经授权的一两天罢工。双方各五人，共十人，围坐在一张桌子旁，桌子对着一块白板。一位中立的主持人询问与会者的想法，并将这些想法记录在白板上。

Facilitator: OK, now let’s see what ideas you have for dealing with this problem of unauthorized work stoppages. Let’s try to get ten ideas on the whiteboard in five minutes. OK, let’s start. Tom?

主持人：好的，现在我们来看看大家对于如何解决未经授权的停工问题有什么想法。请大家在五分钟内尽量在白板上写下十个想法。好的，开始吧。汤姆？

Tom (Union): Foremen ought to be able to settle a union member’s grievance on the spot.

汤姆（工会）：工头应该能够当场解决工会成员的申诉。

Facilitator: Good, I’ve got it down. Jim, you’ve got your hand up.

主持人：很好，我记住了。吉姆，你举手吧。

Jim (Management): A union member ought to talk to his foreman about a problem before taking any action that—

吉姆（管理层）：工会成员在采取任何行动之前，应该先和工头谈谈问题——

Tom (Union): They do, but the foremen don’t listen.

汤姆（工会）：他们确实有，但是工头们不听。

Facilitator: Tom, please, no criticizing yet. We agreed to postpone that until later, OK? How about you, Jerry? You look like you’ve got an idea.

主持人：汤姆，请先别批评。我们之前说好把这件事推迟到以后再说，好吗？杰瑞，你呢？你看上去好像有什么想法。

Jerry (Unlon): When a strike issue comes up, the union members should be allowed to meet in the bathhouse immediately.

杰瑞（Unlon）：当出现罢工问题时，应该允许工会成员立即在澡堂开会。

Roger (Management): Management could agree to let the bathhouse be used for union meetings and could assure the employees’ privacy by shutting the doors and keeping the foremen out.

罗杰（管理层）：管理层可以同意将浴室用作工会会议场所，并通过关闭浴室大门和阻止工头进入来保证员工的隐私。

Carol (Management): How about adopting the rule that there will be no strike without giving the union leaders and management a chance to work it out on the spot?

卡罗尔（管理层）：不如这样，先给工会领导人和管理层一个当场解决问题的机会，然后再进行罢工？

Jerry (Union): How about speeding up the grievance procedure and having a meeting within twenty-four hours if the foreman and union member don’t settle it between themselves?

杰瑞（工会）：如果工头和工会成员不能自行解决问题，能否加快申诉程序，在 24 小时内举行会议？

Karen (Union): Yeah. And how about organizing some joint training for the union members and the foremen on how to handle their problems together?

凯伦（工会）：是啊。不如组织一些工会成员和工头之间的联合培训，教教他们如何共同解决问题？

PhiI (Union): If a person does a good job, let him know it.

PhiI（工会）：如果一个人工作做得好，就让他知道。

John (Management): Establish friendly relations between union people and management people.

约翰（管理层）：建立工会人员与管理层人员之间的友好关系。

Facilitator: That sounds promising, John, but could you be more specific?

主持人：约翰，这听起来很有希望，但你能说得更具体些吗？

John (Management): Well, how about organizing a union–management softball team?

约翰（管理层）：那我们何不组织一支工会-管理层垒球队呢？

Tom (Union): And a bowling team too.

汤姆（联盟）：还有一支保龄球队。

Roger (Management): How about an annual picnic get-together for all the families?

罗杰（管理层）：不如每年举办一次家庭野餐聚会？

And on it goes, as the participants brainstorm lots of ideas. Many of the ideas might never have come up except in such a brainstorming session, and some of them may prove effective in reducing unauthorized strikes. Time spent brainstorming together is surely among the best-spent time in negotiation.

就这样，大家集思广益，提出了许多想法。许多想法或许只有在这样的头脑风暴会议上才会出现，而其中一些想法可能确实能有效减少未经授权的罢工。共同进行头脑风暴无疑是谈判中最有价值的环节之一。

But whether you brainstorm together or not, separating the act of developing options from the act of deciding on them is extremely useful in any negotiation. Discussing options differs radically from taking positions. Whereas one side’s position will conflict with another’s, options invite other options. The very language you use differs. It consists of questions, not assertions; it is open, not closed: “One option is . . . . What other options have you thought of?” “What if we agreed to this?” “How about doing it this way?” “How would this work?” “What would be wrong with that?” Invent before you decide.

但无论你们是否一起集思广益，在任何谈判中，将提出方案和最终决定方案分开都极其重要。讨论方案与表明立场截然不同。一方的立场必然会与另一方的立场相冲突，而方案本身则会引发更多选择。你们使用的语言也不同。方案由问题构成，而非断言；方案是开放式的，而非封闭式的：“一个方案是……你们还想到了哪些其他方案？”“如果我们同意这个方案呢？”“这样做怎么样？”“这样做行得通吗？”“这样做有什么问题？”在做决定之前，先构思方案。

Broaden your options

拓宽你的选择

Even with the best of intentions, participants in a brainstorming session are likely to operate on the assumption that they are really looking for the one best answer, trying to find a needle in a haystack by picking up every blade of hay.

即使出于最好的意愿，头脑风暴会议的参与者也可能认为他们真正想要找到的是唯一最佳答案，就像大海捞针一样，把每一根干草都捡起来。

At this stage in a negotiation, however, you should not be looking for the right path. You are developing room within which to negotiate. Room can be made only by having a substantial number of markedly different ideas—ideas on which you and the other side can build later in the negotiation, and among which you can then jointly choose.

然而，在谈判的这个阶段，你不应该寻找正确的路径。你正在做的是为谈判创造空间。而创造空间的唯一途径是拥有大量截然不同的想法——这些想法可以作为你和对方在后续谈判中共同构建的基础，并最终由双方共同做出选择。

A vintner making a fine wine chooses his grapes from a number of varieties. A sports team looking for star players will send talent scouts to scour the local leagues and college teams all over the nation. The same principle applies to negotiation. The key to wise decision-making, whether in wine-making, sports, or negotiation, lies in selecting from a great number and variety of options.

酿酒师酿造优质葡萄酒时，会从众多葡萄品种中挑选。体育队寻找明星球员时，会派出球探走遍全国各地的联赛和大学球队。同样的道理也适用于谈判。无论是酿酒、体育还是谈判，明智决策的关键都在于从众多且多样化的选项中做出选择。

If you were asked who should receive the Nobel Peace Prize this year, you would do well to answer “Well, let’s think about it” and generate a list of about a hundred names from diplomacy, business, journalism, religion, law, agriculture, politics, academia, medicine, and other fields, making sure to dream up a lot of wild ideas. You would almost certainly end up with a better decision this way than if you tried to decide right from the start.

如果有人问你今年的诺贝尔和平奖应该颁给谁，你最好回答“嗯，让我们想想”，然后列出大约一百个名字，涵盖外交、商业、新闻、宗教、法律、农业、政治、学术、医学等各个领域，务必尽可能多地提出一些天马行空的想法。这样一来，你最终得到的答案几乎肯定会比一开始就急于决定要好得多。

A brainstorming session frees people to think creatively. Once freed, they need ways to think about their problems and to generate constructive solutions.

头脑风暴能激发人们的创造性思维。一旦思维解放，他们就需要找到思考问题并提出建设性解决方案的方法。

Multiply options by shuttling between the specific and the general: The Circle Chart. The task of inventing options involves four types of thinking. One is thinking about a particular problem—the factual situation you dislike, for example, a smelly, polluted river that runs by your land. The second type of thinking is descriptive analysis—you diagnose an existing situation in general terms. You sort problems into categories and tentatively suggest causes. The river water may have a high content of various chemicals, or too little oxygen. You may suspect various upstream industrial plants. The third type of thinking, again in general terms, is to consider what ought, perhaps, to be done. Given the diagnoses you have made, you look for prescriptions that theory may suggest, such as reducing chemical effluent, reducing diversions of water, or bringing fresh water from some other river. The fourth and final type of thinking is to come up with some specific and feasible suggestions for action. Who might do what tomorrow to put one of these general approaches into practice? For instance, the state environmental agency might order an upstream industry to limit the quantity of chemical discharge.

通过在具体和一般之间切换来增加选择：圆形图。构思方案需要四种思维方式。第一种是思考具体问题——例如，你不喜欢的实际情况，比如流经你土地的一条散发恶臭、污染严重的河流。第二种思维方式是描述性分析——你用概括性的语言诊断现有情况。你将问题分类，并初步提出原因。河水可能含有大量各种化学物质，或者氧气含量过低。你可能怀疑上游的某些工业工厂。第三种思维方式，同样是概括性的，是考虑或许应该采取什么措施。根据你做出的诊断，你寻找理论可能提出的解决方案，例如减少化学废水排放、减少引水或从其他河流引水。第四种也是最后一种思维方式是提出一些具体可行的行动建议。明天谁可以采取什么行动来将这些一般性方法付诸实践？例如，州环保机构可能会责令上游企业限制化学品排放量。

The Circle Chart on the next page illustrates these four types of thinking and suggests them as steps to be taken in sequence. If all goes well, the specific action invented in this way will, if adopted, deal with your original problem.

下一页的圆形图展示了这四种思维方式，并建议按顺序采取这些步骤。如果一切顺利，按照这种方式制定的具体行动方案一旦实施，就能解决你最初的问题。

The Circle Chart provides an easy way of using one good idea to generate others. With one useful action idea before you, you (or a group of you who are brainstorming) can go back and try to identify the general approach of which the action idea is merely one application. You can then think up other action ideas that would apply the same general approach to the real world. Similarly, you can go back one step further and ask, “If this theoretical approach appears useful, what is the diagnosis behind it?” Having articulated a diagnosis, you can generate other approaches for dealing with a problem analyzed in that way, and then look for actions putting these new approaches into practice. One good option on the table thus opens the door to asking about the theory that makes this option good and then using that theory to invent more options.

圆形图提供了一种简便的方法，可以利用一个好想法来激发更多想法。当你面前有一个有用的行动方案时，你（或参与头脑风暴的小组）可以回过头来，尝试找出该方案所依据的总体方法，而该方案仅仅是该方法的一种应用。然后，你可以思考其他将相同总体方法应用于现实世界的行动方案。同样地，你可以更进一步，问自己：“如果这种理论方法看起来有用，那么它背后的诊断是什么？” 明确了诊断之后，你可以针对以这种方式分析的问题，提出其他解决方案，然后寻找将这些新方案付诸实践的行动。因此，一个好的方案就为探究其背后的理论打开了大门，并可以运用该理论来创造更多方案。

An example may illustrate the process. In thinking about how to deal with the conflict in Northern Ireland, one idea generated in the 1980s was to have Catholic and Protestant teachers prepare a common workbook on the history of Northern Ireland for use in the primary grades of both school systems. The book, which was actually created and used in the 1990s, presents Northern Irish history as seen from different points of view and gives the children exercises that involve role-playing and putting themselves in other people’s shoes. More useful ideas were then generated by starting with this specific action suggestion and asking what theoretical approaches underlay it. This resulted in such general propositions as:

举例说明这个过程。在思考如何应对北爱尔兰冲突时，20世纪80年代提出的一个想法是，让天主教和新教教师共同编写一本关于北爱尔兰历史的练习册，供两个学区的小学低年级学生使用。这本练习册在20世纪90年代实际编写并投入使用，它从不同的视角呈现了北爱尔兰的历史，并为孩子们提供了角色扮演和换位思考的练习。随后，人们从这个具体的行动建议出发，探究其背后的理论方法，从而产生了更多有用的想法。最终得出了一些普遍性的命题，例如：

“There should be some common educational content in the two school systems.”

“这两个教育体系应该有一些共同的教育内容。”

“Catholics and Protestants should work together on small, manageable projects.”

“天主教徒和新教徒应该在小型、可控的项目上合作。”

“Understanding should be promoted in young children before it is too late.”

“应该在为时过晚之前，帮助幼儿培养理解能力。”

“History should be taught in ways that illuminate partisan perceptions.”

“历史教学应该以能够阐明党派观念的方式进行。”

Working from these theories additional action suggestions were invented, including a joint Catholic and Protestant film project that presents the history of Northern Ireland as seen through different eyes, a teacher exchange program, and having some common classes for primary-age children in the two systems.

基于这些理论，又提出了一些行动建议，包括天主教和新教联合拍摄电影，从不同的视角展现北爱尔兰的历史；教师交流计划；以及为两个教育体系中的小学生开设一些共同课程。

Look through the eyes of different experts. Another way to generate multiple options is to examine your problem from the perspective of different professions and disciplines.

换位思考，从不同专家的角度看待问题。另一种产生多种方案的方法是，从不同职业和学科的角度审视你的问题。

In thinking up possible solutions to a dispute over custody of a child, for example, look at the problem as it might be seen by an educator, a banker, a psychiatrist, a civil rights lawyer, a minister, a nutritionist, a doctor, a feminist, a football coach, or one with some other special point of view. If you are negotiating a business contract, invent options that might occur to a banker, an inventor, a labor leader, a speculator in real estate, a stockbroker, an economist, a tax expert, or a socialist.

例如，在思考如何解决子女监护权纠纷时，可以尝试从教育工作者、银行家、精神科医生、民权律师、牧师、营养师、医生、女权主义者、足球教练或其他具有特殊视角的人的角度来审视这个问题。如果你正在协商商业合同，可以设想一下银行家、发明家、工会领袖、房地产投机者、股票经纪人、经济学家、税务专家或社会主义者可能会想到的方案。

You can also combine the use of the Circle Chart with this idea of looking at a problem through the eyes of different experts. Consider in turn how each expert would diagnose the situation, what kinds of approaches each might suggest, and what practical suggestions would follow from those approaches.

你还可以将圆形图的使用与从不同专家的角度看待问题的思路结合起来。依次思考每位专家会如何诊断情况，他们可能会提出哪些方法，以及这些方法会衍生出哪些切实可行的建议。

Invent agreements of different strengths. You can multiply the number of possible agreements on the table by thinking of “weaker” versions you might want to have on hand in case a sought-for agreement proves beyond reach. If you cannot agree on substance, perhaps you can agree on procedure. If a shoe factory cannot agree with a wholesaler on who should pay for a shipment of damaged shoes, perhaps they can agree to submit the issue to an arbitrator. Similarly, where a permanent agreement is not possible, perhaps a provisional agreement is. At the very least, if you and the other side cannot reach first-order agreement, you can usually reach second-order agreement—that is, agree on where you disagree, so that you both know the issues in dispute, which are not always obvious. The pairs of adjectives below suggest potential agreements of differing “strengths”:

制定不同强度的协议。您可以考虑制定一些“较弱”的协议版本，以备不时之需，避免达成无法实现的实质性协议。如果无法就实质内容达成一致，或许可以就程序达成一致。例如，如果鞋厂和批发商无法就受损鞋的赔偿责任达成一致，或许可以同意将争议提交仲裁。同样，如果无法达成永久性协议，或许可以达成临时协议。至少，如果双方无法达成初步协议，通常可以达成次级协议——即就分歧所在达成一致，从而明确双方的争议焦点，而这些争议焦点并非总是显而易见的。以下形容词组合可以提示不同“强度”的潜在协议：

Stronger

更强壮

Weaker

较弱

Substantive

实质性

Procedural

程序

Permanent

永恒的

Provisional

临时

Comprehensive

综合的

Partial

部分的

Final

最终的

In principle

原则

Unconditional

无条件

Contingent

队伍

Binding

结合

Nonbinding

非约束性

First-order

一阶

Second-order

二阶

Change the scope of a proposed agreement. Consider the possibility of varying not only the strength of the agreement but also its scope. You could, for instance, “fractionate” your problem into smaller and perhaps more manageable units. To a prospective editor for your book, you might suggest: “How about editing the first chapter for $300, and we’ll see how it goes?” Agreements may be partial, involve fewer parties, cover only selected subject matters, apply only to a certain geographical area, or remain in effect for only a limited period of time.

改变拟议协议的范围。考虑调整协议的效力以及范围。例如，您可以将问题“分解”成更小、更易于管理的部分。您可以对潜在的图书编辑建议：“第一章的编辑费用是 300 美元，我们看看效果如何？” 协议可以是部分性的，涉及的当事方可以较少，协议内容可以仅限于特定主题，协议的适用范围可以仅限于特定地理区域，或者协议的有效期也可以是有限的。

It is also provocative to ask how the subject matter might be enlarged so as to “sweeten the pot” and make agreement more attractive. The dispute between India and Pakistan over the waters of the Indus River became more amenable to settlement when the World Bank entered the discussions; the parties were challenged to invent new irrigation projects, new storage dams, and other engineering works for the benefit of both nations, all to be funded with the assistance of the Bank.

同样引人深思的是，如何扩大议题范围，以“增加吸引力”，使协议更具吸引力。印度和巴基斯坦之间关于印度河水资源的争端，在世界银行介入谈判后，更容易得到解决；双方被要求设计新的灌溉工程、新的蓄水坝和其他工程项目，以造福两国，所有这些项目都将由世界银行提供资金。

Look for mutual gain

寻求互利共赢

The third major block to creative problem-solving lies in the assumption of a fixed pie: the less for you, the more for me. Rarely if ever is this assumption true. First of all, both sides can always be worse off than they are now. Chess looks like a zero-sum game; if one loses, the other wins—until a dog trots by and knocks over the table, spills the beer, and leaves you both worse off than before.

阻碍创造性问题解决的第三个主要障碍在于“蛋糕是固定的”这种假设：你分得的越少，我分得的就越多。这种假设几乎从未成立。首先，双方的处境总有可能比现在更糟。下棋看起来像是零和博弈；一方输了，另一方就赢了——直到一只狗跑过来，掀翻了桌子，打翻了啤酒，让双方的处境都比之前更糟。

Even apart from a shared interest in averting joint loss, there almost always exists the possibility of joint gain. This may take the form of developing a mutually advantageous relationship, or of satisfying the interests of each side with a creative solution.

即使撇开避免共同损失的共同利益不谈，几乎总存在共同获益的可能性。这可能表现为建立互利共赢的关系，或者通过创造性的解决方案满足双方的利益。

Identify shared interests. In theory it is obvious that shared interests help produce agreement. By definition, inventing an idea that meets shared interests is good for you and good for them. In practice, however, the picture seems less clear. In the middle of a negotiation over price, shared interests may not appear obvious or relevant. How then can looking for shared interests help?

找出共同利益。理论上，共同利益显然有助于达成协议。从定义上讲，提出一个符合共同利益的想法对你和对方都有好处。然而，在实践中，情况似乎并非如此简单。在价格谈判过程中，共同利益可能并不明显或相关。那么，寻找共同利益究竟有何帮助呢？

Let’s take an example. Suppose you are the manager of an oil refinery. Call it Townsend Oil. The mayor of Pageville, the city where the refinery is located, has told you he wants to raise the taxes Townsend Oil pays to Pageville from two million dollars a year to four million. You have told him that you think two million a year is quite sufficient. The negotiation stands there: he wants more, you want to pay what you have been paying. In this negotiation, a typical one in many ways, where do shared interests come into play?

我们举个例子。假设你是一家炼油厂的经理，我们称之为汤森石油公司。炼油厂所在的帕吉维尔市市长告诉你，他想把汤森石油公司每年向帕吉维尔市缴纳的税款从两百万美元提高到四百万美元。你告诉他，你认为每年两百万美元已经足够了。谈判陷入僵局：他想要更多，你只想支付你一直以来缴纳的税款。在这场谈判中——这场谈判在很多方面都很典型——双方的共同利益在哪里发挥作用呢？

Let’s take a closer look at what the mayor wants. He wants money—money undoubtedly to pay for city services, a new civic center, perhaps, and to relieve the ordinary taxpayers. But the city cannot obtain all the money it needs for now and for the future just from Townsend Oil. They will look for money from the petrochemical plant across the street, for example, and, for the future, from new businesses and from the expansion of existing businesses. The mayor, a businessman himself, would also like to encourage industrial expansion and attract new businesses that will provide new jobs and strengthen Pageville’s economy.

让我们仔细看看市长想要什么。他想要钱——无疑是用来支付市政服务、新建市民中心，以及减轻普通纳税人的负担。但是，这座城市不可能仅靠汤森石油公司就能获得现在和未来所需的所有资金。例如，他们会寻求街对面石化厂的资金，而未来则需要依靠新企业和现有企业的扩张。市长本人也是一位商人，他希望鼓励工业扩张，吸引能够创造新就业机会、增强佩奇维尔经济实力的新企业。

What are your company’s interests? Given the rapid changes in the technology of refining oil, and the antiquated condition of your refinery, you are presently considering a major refurbishment and expansion of the plant. You are concerned that the city may later increase its assessment of the value of the expanded refinery, thus making taxes even higher. Consider also that you have been encouraging a plastics plant to locate itself nearby to make convenient use of your product. Naturally, you worry that the plastics plant will have second thoughts once they see the city increasing taxes.

贵公司的利益是什么？鉴于炼油技术的快速发展以及贵公司炼油厂的陈旧状况，您目前正在考虑对工厂进行大规模的翻新和扩建。您担心市政府日后可能会提高扩建后炼油厂的估值，从而导致税收进一步增加。此外，您一直在鼓励一家塑料厂选址附近，以便方便地使用贵公司的产品。当然，您也担心塑料厂一旦看到市政府提高税收，就会重新考虑是否选址。

The shared interests between the mayor and you now become more apparent. You both agree on the goals of fostering industrial expansion and encouraging new industries. If you did some inventing to meet these shared goals, you might come up with several ideas: a tax holiday of seven years for new industries, a joint publicity campaign with the Chamber of Commerce to attract new companies, a reduction in taxes for existing industries that choose to expand. Such ideas might save you money while still filling the city’s coffers. If on the other hand the negotiation soured the relationship between company and town, both would lose. You might cut back on your corporate contributions to city charities and school athletics. The city might become unreasonably tough in enforcing the building code and other ordinances. Your personal relationship with the city’s political and business leaders might grow unpleasant. The relationship between the sides, often taken for granted and overlooked, frequently outweighs in importance the outcome of any particular issue.

您和市长之间的共同利益现在变得更加明显。你们都认同促进工业扩张和鼓励新兴产业的目标。如果您能发挥创造力来实现这些共同目标，您可能会提出一些想法：例如，为新兴产业提供七年的免税期；与商会联合开展宣传活动以吸引新公司；以及为选择扩张的现有企业减税。这些想法或许能为您省钱，同时也能充实市财政。但另一方面，如果谈判导致公司与市政府关系恶化，双方都将蒙受损失。您可能会减少公司对市政府慈善机构和学校体育项目的捐款。市政府可能会在执行建筑规范和其他法令方面采取过于强硬的措施。您与市政府政商界领袖的私人关系也可能变得不愉快。双方之间的关系往往被人们视为理所当然和忽视，但其重要性通常超过任何具体问题的结果。

As a negotiator, you will almost always want to look for solutions that will leave the other side satisfied as well. If the customer feels cheated in a purchase, the store owner has also failed; he may lose a customer and his reputation may suffer. An outcome in which the other side gets absolutely nothing is worse for you than one that leaves them mollified. In almost every case, your satisfaction depends to a degree on making the other side sufficiently content with an agreement to want to live up to it.

作为谈判者，你几乎总是希望找到能让对方也满意的解决方案。如果顾客感觉在购物中被欺骗，那么店主也同样失败了；他可能会失去一位顾客，声誉也会受损。让对方一无所获的结果，对你来说比让他们感到满意的结果更糟糕。几乎在所有情况下，你的满意度都在一定程度上取决于你是否能让对方对协议感到足够满意，并愿意履行协议。

Three points about shared interests are worth remembering. First, shared interests lie latent in every negotiation. They may not be immediately obvious. Ask yourself: Do we have a shared interest in preserving our relationship? What opportunities lie ahead for cooperation and mutual benefit? What costs would we bear if negotiations broke off? Are there common principles, like a fair price, that we both can respect?

关于共同利益，有三点值得牢记。首先，共同利益潜藏于每一次谈判之中，它们或许并不显而易见。不妨问问自己：我们是否都希望维护彼此的关系？未来有哪些合作互利的机会？如果谈判破裂，我们将承担哪些代价？是否存在双方都能尊重的共同原则，例如公平的价格？

Second, shared interests are opportunities, not godsends. To be of use, you need to make something out of them. It helps to make a shared interest explicit and to formulate it as a shared goal. In other words, make it concrete and future-oriented. As manager of Townsend Oil, for example, you could set a joint goal with the mayor of bringing five new industries into Pageville within three years. The tax holiday for new industries would then represent not a concession by the mayor to you but an action in pursuit of your shared goal.

其次，共同利益是机遇，而非天赐良机。要想发挥作用，你需要将其转化为实际成果。明确共同利益并将其转化为共同目标至关重要。换句话说，要使其具体化并面向未来。例如，作为汤森石油公司的经理，你可以与市长共同设定一个目标：在三年内为佩奇维尔市引进五家新企业。这样一来，市长为新企业提供的税收优惠就不是对你的让步，而是为实现你们共同目标而采取的行动。

Third, stressing your shared interests can make the negotiation smoother and more amicable. Passengers in a lifeboat afloat in the middle of the ocean with limited rations will subordinate their differences over food in pursuit of their shared interest in getting to shore.

第三，强调共同利益可以使谈判更加顺利友好。就像在茫茫大海中漂流的救生艇上，食物有限，乘客们为了到达岸边的共同目标，会暂时搁置对食物的分歧一样。

Dovetail differing interests. Consider once again the two children quarreling over an orange. Each child wanted the orange, so they split it, failing to realize that one wanted only the fruit to eat and the other only the peel for baking. In this case as in many others, a satisfactory agreement is made possible because each side wants different things. This is genuinely startling if you think about it. People generally assume that differences between two parties create the problem. Yet differences can also lead to a solution.

巧妙地调和不同利益。再想想两个孩子争抢一个橙子的情景。他们都想要这个橙子，于是分了它，却没意识到一个孩子只想吃果肉，另一个孩子只想用橙皮做烘焙。在这个例子中，就像在很多其他例子中一样，双方的需求不同，最终达成令人满意的协议。仔细想想，这确实令人惊讶。人们通常认为，双方的差异是问题的根源。然而，差异也可以带来解决方案。

Agreement is often based on disagreement. It is as absurd to think, for example, that you should always begin by reaching agreement on the facts as it is for a buyer of stock to try to convince the seller that the stock is likely to go up. If they did agree that the stock would go up, the seller would probably not sell. What makes a deal likely is that the buyer believes the price will go up and the seller believes it will go down. The difference in belief provides the basis for a deal.

协议往往建立在分歧之上。例如，认为应该总是先就事实达成一致，就像股票买家试图说服卖家股票可能会上涨一样荒谬。如果他们真的都认为股票会上涨，卖家可能就不会卖了。促成交易的关键在于买家相信价格会上涨，而卖家相信价格会下跌。这种信念上的差异构成了交易的基础。

Many creative agreements reflect this principle of reaching agreement through differences. Differences in interests and belief make it possible for an item to be of high benefit to you, yet low cost to the other side. Consider the nursery rhyme:

许多富有创意的协议都体现了通过差异达成共识的原则。利益和信仰的差异使得某项事物对你而言可能获益良多，而对对方而言成本却很低。想想这首童谣：

Jack Sprat could eat no fat

杰克·斯普拉特不能吃脂肪

His wife could eat no lean,

他的妻子不能吃瘦肉，

And so betwixt them both

于是，他们两人之间就产生了这种关系。

They licked the platter clean.

他们把盘子舔得干干净净。

The kinds of differences that best lend themselves to dovetailing are differences in interests, in beliefs, in the value placed on time, in forecasts, and in aversion to risk.

最容易相互契合的差异是兴趣、信仰、对时间的重视程度、预测以及对风险的厌恶程度方面的差异。

Any difference in interests? The following brief checklist suggests common variations in interest to look for:

兴趣方面有差异吗？以下简要清单列出了一些常见的兴趣差异，供您参考：

One party cares more about:

一方更关心：

The other party cares more about:

对方更关心的是：

Form

形式

Substance

物质

Economic considerations

经济因素

Political considerations

政治因素

Internal considerations

内部因素

External considerations

外部因素

Symbolic considerations

象征意义的考量

Practical considerations

实际考虑因素

Immediate future

不久的将来

More distant future

更遥远的未来

Ad hoc results

临时结果

The relationship

这种关系

Hardware

硬件

Ideology

思想

Progress

进步

Respect for tradition

尊重传统

Precedent

先例

This case

本案

Prestige, reputation

声望，声誉

Results

结果

Political points

政治要点

Group welfare

团体福利

Different beliefs? If I believe I’m right, and you believe you’re right, we can take advantage of this difference in beliefs. We may both agree to have an impartial arbitrator settle the issue, each confident of victory. If two factions of the union leadership cannot agree on a certain wage proposal, they can agree to submit the issue to a membership vote.

信念不同？如果我认为自己是对的，你也认为你是对的，我们可以利用这种信念差异。我们双方都可以同意由一位公正的仲裁员来解决问题，并且都对胜诉充满信心。如果工会领导层的两个派别无法就某项工资提案达成一致，他们可以同意将这个问题提交给全体会员投票表决。

Different values placed on time? You may care more about the present while the other side cares more about the future. In the language of business, you discount future value at different rates. An installment plan works on this principle. The buyer is willing to pay a higher price for a car if it is possible to pay over time; the seller is willing to accept payment later for a higher price.

对时间的价值判断不同？你可能更看重当下，而对方则更看重未来。用商业术语来说，未来价值的折现率不同。分期付款计划正是基于这个原理。如果可以分期付款，买家愿意支付更高的价格；卖家也愿意接受更高的价格，但允许买家稍后付款。

Different forecasts? In a salary negotiation between an aging football star and a major team, the player may expect to win a lot of games while the team owner has the opposite expectation. Taking advantage of these different expectations, they might both agree on a modest base salary plus a big bonus if the team makes the playoffs.

不同的预期？在一位年迈的足球明星与一支豪门球队的薪资谈判中，球员可能期望球队赢得很多比赛，而球队老板则抱有相反的预期。利用这种预期差异，双方或许可以达成一致：一份适中的基本工资，外加球队打进季后赛时的一笔丰厚奖金。

Differences in aversion to risk? One last kind of difference that you may capitalize on is aversion to risk. Take, for example, the issue of deep-seabed mining that arose in international Law of the Sea negotiations. How much should mining companies pay the international community for the privilege of mining minerals from the seabed in international waters? The mining companies care more about avoiding big losses than they do about making big gains. For them deep-seabed mining is a major investment. They want to reduce the risk. The international community, on the other hand, is concerned with revenue. If some company is going to make a lot of money out of “the common heritage of mankind,” the rest of the world wants a generous share.

风险厌恶程度的差异？您可以利用的最后一种差异是风险厌恶程度。例如，在国际海洋法谈判中出现的深海采矿问题。矿业公司应该为在国际水域海底开采矿物的特权向国际社会支付多少费用？矿业公司更关心的是避免巨额损失，而不是获得巨额收益。对他们来说，深海采矿是一项重大投资。他们希望降低风险。另一方面，国际社会则关注收益。如果某家公司要从“人类共同遗产”中赚取巨额利润，那么世界其他国家都希望获得丰厚的回报。

In this difference lies the potential for a bargain advantageous to both sides. Risk can be traded for revenue. Exploiting this difference in aversion to risk, the resulting treaty provides for charging the companies low rates until they recover their investment—in other words, while their risk is high—and much higher rates thereafter, when their risk is low.

这种差异蕴含着达成对双方都有利的交易的可能。风险可以转化为收益。利用双方对风险厌恶程度的差异，最终达成的条约规定，在公司收回投资之前（即风险较高时），对它们收取较低的税率；而在风险较低之后，则收取更高的税率。

Ask for their preferences. One way to dovetail interests is to invent several options all equally acceptable to you and ask the other side which one they prefer. You want to know what is preferable, not necessarily what is acceptable. You can then take that option, work with it some more, and again present two or more variants, asking which one they prefer. In this way, without anyone’s making a decision, you can improve a plan until you can find no more joint gains. For example, the agent for the sports star might ask the team owner: “What meets your interests better, a salary of $8.75 million a year for four years, or $10 million a year for three years? The latter? OK, how about between that and $7.5 million a year for three years with a $10 million bonus in each year that Fernando is voted MVP or the team wins the championship?”

询问对方的偏好。一种协调双方利益的方法是，拟定几个你认为同样可以接受的方案，然后询问对方更喜欢哪一个。你想知道的是哪个方案更可取，而不仅仅是哪个方案可以接受。之后，你可以选择这个方案，进一步完善，再次提出两个或多个变体，询问对方更喜欢哪一个。这样，在双方都未做出决定的情况下，你可以不断改进方案，直到找到双方都能从中获益的方案为止。例如，体育明星的经纪人可能会问球队老板：“四年每年875万美元的薪水，还是三年每年1000万美元的薪水，哪个更符合您的利益？后者？好的，那么在两者之间，如果费尔南多获得最有价值球员奖或球队赢得总冠军，每年额外获得1000万美元的奖金，您觉得哪个更好？”

If dovetailing had to be summed up in one sentence, it would be: Look for items that are of low cost to you and high benefit to them, and vice versa. Differences in interests, priorities, beliefs, forecasts, and attitudes toward risk all make dovetailing possible. A negotiator’s motto could be “Vive la différence!”

如果要用一句话概括“协同效应”，那就是：寻找对你成本低、对对方收益高的资源，反之亦然。利益、优先事项、信念、预测以及风险态度上的差异，都使得协同效应成为可能。谈判者的座右铭或许可以写成“差异万岁！”

Make their decision easy

让他们更容易做出决定

Since success for you in a negotiation depends upon the other side’s making a decision you want, you should do what you can to make that decision an easy one. Rather than make things difficult for the other side, you want to confront them with a choice that is as painless as possible. Impressed with the merits of their own case, people usually pay too little attention to ways of advancing their case by taking care of interests on the other side. To overcome the shortsightedness that results from looking too narrowly at one’s immediate self-interest, you will want to put yourself in their shoes. Without some option that appeals to them, there is likely to be no agreement at all.

谈判的成功取决于对方是否做出你希望的决定，因此你应该尽力让对方更容易做出决定。与其让对方感到为难，不如让他们面对一个尽可能轻松的选择。人们往往过于关注自身利益，而忽略了如何通过顾及对方的利益来推进自己的立场。为了克服这种目光短浅、只顾眼前利益的思维方式，你需要设身处地地为对方着想。如果没有对方能够接受的选项，双方很可能根本无法达成协议。

Whose shoes? Are you trying to influence a single negotiator, an absent boss, or some committee or other collective decision-making body? You cannot negotiate successfully with an abstraction like “Houston” or “the University of California.” Instead of trying to persuade “the insurance company” to make a decision, it is wiser to focus your efforts on getting one claims agent to make a recommendation. However complex the other side’s decisional process may seem, you will understand it better if you pick one person—probably the person with whom you are dealing—and see how the problem looks from his or her point of view.

谁的立场？你是想影响某个谈判代表、缺席的老板，还是某个委员会或其他集体决策机构？你不可能与“休斯顿”或“加州大学”这样的抽象概念进行成功的谈判。与其试图说服“保险公司”做出决定，不如将精力集中在争取一位理赔员提出建议上。无论对方的决策过程看起来多么复杂，如果你选择一个人——很可能就是你正在与之沟通的人——并从他/她的角度看待问题，你就能更好地理解它。

By focusing on one person you are not ignoring complexities. Rather, you are handling them by understanding how they impinge on the person with whom you are negotiating. You may come to appreciate your negotiating role in a new light, and see your job, for example, as strengthening that person’s hand or giving her arguments that she will need to persuade others to go along. One British ambassador described his job as “helping my opposite number get new instructions.” If you place yourself firmly in the shoes of your opposite number, you will understand his problem and what kind of options might solve it.

专注于某个人并不意味着忽略了问题的复杂性。相反，你通过理解这些问题如何影响与你谈判的人来处理它们。你可能会对自己的谈判角色有新的认识，例如，你会将自己的工作视为增强对方的谈判筹码，或者为她提供说服他人所需的论据。一位英国大使曾将他的工作描述为“帮助对方获得新的指示”。如果你能设身处地地站在对方的角度思考，你就能理解他的问题以及可能的解决方案。

What decision? In Chapter 2 we discussed how one can understand the other side’s interests by analyzing their currently perceived choice. Now you are trying to generate options that will so change their choice that they might then decide in a way satisfactory to you. Your task is to give them not a problem but an answer, to give them not a tough decision but an easy one. It is crucial in that process to focus your attention on the content of the decision itself. That decision is often impeded by uncertainty.

什么决定？第二章我们讨论了如何通过分析对方当前所感知的选择来理解他们的利益。现在，你要尝试提出一些方案，这些方案能够彻底改变他们的选择，使他们最终做出令你满意的决定。你的任务不是给他们一个难题，而是给他们一个答案；不是给他们一个艰难的决定，而是一个简单的决定。在这个过程中，至关重要的是要将注意力集中在决策本身的内容上。而决策往往会受到不确定性的阻碍。

Frequently you want as much as you can get, but you yourself do not know how much that is. You are likely to say, in effect, “Come up with something and I will tell you if it is enough.” That may seem reasonable to you, but when you look at it from the other’s point of view, you will understand the need to invent a more appealing request. For whatever they do or say, you are likely to consider that merely a floor—and ask for more. Requesting the other side to be “more forthcoming” will probably not produce a decision you want.

你常常想要尽可能多的东西，但你自己却不知道到底多少才够。你很可能会说：“你先想个办法，我再告诉你够不够。” 你觉得这似乎合情合理，但如果你站在对方的角度思考，就会明白你需要提出一个更有吸引力的要求。无论他们做什么或说什么，你都可能认为那只是底线——然后要求更多。要求对方“更坦诚”很可能不会得到你想要的结果。

Many negotiators are uncertain whether they are asking for words or for performance. Yet the distinction is critical. If it is performance you want, do not add something for “negotiating room.” If you want a horse to jump a fence, don’t raise the fence. If you want to sell a soft drink from a vending machine for $2.00, don’t mark the price at $2.50 to give yourself room to negotiate.

许多谈判者并不确定自己究竟是在要求对方说出承诺的话，还是要求对方拿出实际行动。然而，区分二者至关重要。如果你想要的是实际行动，就不要为了“留有谈判空间”而增加条件。如果你想让马跳过栅栏，就不要把栅栏建高。如果你想以2美元的价格从自动售货机出售软饮料，就不要为了给自己留有谈判空间而把价格标为2.5美元。

Most of the time you will want a promise—an agreement. Take a pencil and paper in hand and try drafting a few possible agreements. It is never too early in a negotiation to start drafting as an aid to clear thinking. Prepare multiple versions, starting with the simplest possible. What are some terms that the other party could sign, terms that would be attractive to them as well as to you? Can you reduce the number of people whose approval would be required? Can you formulate an agreement that will be easy for them to implement? The other side will take into account difficulties in carrying out an agreement; you should too.

大多数时候，你需要的是一个承诺——一份协议。拿起纸笔，尝试起草几个可能的协议。谈判初期就开始起草协议，有助于理清思路，永远不会太早。准备多个版本，从最简单的开始。对方可以签署哪些条款？哪些条款对他们和你都有吸引力？能否减少需要批准的人数？能否制定一份他们易于执行的协议？对方会考虑执行协议的难点，你也应该考虑。

It is usually easier, for example, to refrain from doing something not being done than to stop action already underway. And it is easier to cease doing something than to undertake an entirely new course of action. If workers want music on the job, it will be easier for the company to agree not to interfere for a few weeks with an experimental employee-run program than for the company to agree to run such a program.

例如，不去做一件目前还没做的事情，通常比停止已经开始的事情要容易得多。停止做某件事也比采取全新的行动方案要容易得多。如果员工希望在工作场所听音乐，公司更容易同意在几周内不干预一项由员工自主发起的实验性项目，而不是同意实施这样一个项目。

Because most people are strongly influenced by their notions of legitimacy, one effective way to develop solutions easy for the other side to accept is to shape them so that they will appear legitimate. The other side is more likely to accept a solution if it seems the right thing to do—right in terms of being fair, legal, honorable, and so forth.

由于大多数人深受合法性观念的影响，因此，要想制定出对方容易接受的解决方案，一个有效的方法就是使其看起来合情合理。如果一个解决方案看起来是正确的——公平、合法、合乎道德等等——那么对方就更有可能接受它。

Few things facilitate a decision as much as precedent. Search for it. Look for a decision or statement that the other side may have made in a similar situation, and try to base a proposed agreement on it. This provides an objective standard for your request and makes it easier for them to go along. Recognizing their probable desire to be consistent, thinking about what they have already done or said will help you generate options acceptable to you that also take their point of view into account.

没有什么比先例更能促进决策了。所以，要寻找先例。寻找对方在类似情况下可能做出的决定或声明，并尝试以此为基础提出协议。这能为你的请求提供一个客观的标准，也更容易让对方接受。考虑到对方可能希望保持一致，思考他们过去的做法或言论将有助于你提出既能兼顾双方利益，又能满足你自身需求的方案。

Making threats is not enough. In addition to the content of the decision you would like them to make, you will want to consider from their point of view the consequences of following that decision. If you were they, what results would you most fear? What would you hope for?

仅仅发出威胁是不够的。除了你想让他们做出的决定的内容之外，你还需要从他们的角度考虑做出该决定的后果。如果你是他们，你最害怕的结果是什么？你希望的结果又是什么？

We often try to influence others by threats and warnings of what will happen if they do not decide as we would like. Offers are usually more effective. Concentrate both on making them aware of the consequences they can expect if they do decide as you wish and on improving those consequences from their point of view. How can you make your offers more credible? What are some specific things that they might like? Would they like to be given credit for having made the final proposal? Would they like to make the announcement? What can you invent that might be attractive to them but low in cost to yourself?

我们常常试图通过威胁和警告来影响他人，告诉他们如果不按我们意愿行事将会发生什么。但通常来说，提出提议更为有效。你应该既要让他们意识到如果按照你的意愿行事可能面临的后果，又要从他们的角度出发，努力改善这些后果。如何才能让你的提议更具说服力？他们可能会喜欢哪些具体的东西？他们是否希望因最终方案的提出而获得认可？他们是否希望由他们来宣布结果？你能想出哪些既能吸引他们又能降低自身成本的方案？

To evaluate an option from the other side’s point of view, consider how they might be criticized if they adopted it. Write out a sentence or two illustrating what the other side’s most powerful critic might say about the decision you are thinking of asking for. Then write out a couple of sentences with which the other side might reply in defense. Such an exercise will help you appreciate the restraints within which the other side is negotiating. It should help you generate options that will adequately meet their interests so that they can make a decision that meets yours.

要从对方的角度评估某个方案，就要考虑如果他们采纳该方案可能会受到哪些批评。写一两句话，说明对方最有力的批评者可能会如何评价你正在考虑提出的决定。然后再写几句话，说明对方可能会如何反驳。这样的练习能帮助你理解对方谈判时所受到的限制。它应该能帮助你提出既能充分满足对方利益，又能让他们做出符合你利益的决定的方案。

A final test of an option is to write it out in the form of a “yesable proposition.” Try to draft a proposal to which their responding with the single word “yes” would be sufficient, realistic, and operational. When you can do so, you will have reduced the risk that your immediate self-interest has blinded you to the necessity of meeting concerns of the other side.

对方案进行最终检验的方法是将其写成一个“可行方案”。尝试拟定一个对方只需回答“是”就足够、切实可行且有效的方案。如果能做到这一点，就能降低因自身利益蒙蔽双眼而忽视对方顾虑的风险。

In a complex situation, creative inventing is an absolute necessity. In any negotiation it may open doors and produce a range of potential agreements satisfactory to each side. Therefore, generate many options before selecting among them. Invent first; decide later. Look for shared interests and differing interests to dovetail. And seek to make their decision easy.

在复杂的情况下，创造性思维至关重要。在任何谈判中，它都能打开局面，并产生一系列双方都能接受的潜在协议。因此，在做出选择之前，要尽可能多地提出方案。先构思，后决策。寻找双方的共同利益和分歧，并努力让对方更容易做出决定。

# ↩

5 Insist on Using Objective Criteria

5. 坚持使用客观标准

H owever well you understand the interests of the other side, however ingeniously you invent ways of reconciling interests, however highly you value an ongoing relationship, you will almost always face the harsh reality of interests that conflict. No talk of “win-win” strategies can conceal that fact. You want the rent to be lower; the landlord wants it to be higher. You want the goods delivered tomorrow; the supplier would rather deliver them next week. You definitely prefer the large office with the view; so does your partner. Such differences cannot be swept under the rug.

无论你多么了解对方的利益，无论你多么巧妙地想出调和利益的方法，无论你多么重视长期的合作关系，你几乎总会面临利益冲突的残酷现实。任何“双赢”策略都无法掩盖这一事实。你想降低房租，房东却想提高。你想明天就收到货，供应商却宁愿下周再送。你更喜欢视野开阔的大办公室，你的伴侣也一样。这些分歧无法被掩盖。

Deciding on the basis of will is costly

仅凭意志做决定代价高昂

Typically, negotiators try to resolve such conflicts by positional bargaining—in other words, by talking about what they are willing and unwilling to accept. One negotiator may demand substantive concessions simply because he insists upon them: “The price is $5,000 and that’s that.” Another may make a generous offer, hoping to gain approval or friendship. Whether the situation becomes a contest over who can be the most stubborn or a contest over who can be the most generous, this negotiating process focuses on what each side is willing to agree to. The outcome results from the interaction of two human wills—almost as if the negotiators were living on a desert island, with no history, no customs, and no moral standards.

通常，谈判者会尝试通过立场谈判来解决此类冲突——换句话说，就是讨论他们愿意接受和不愿意接受的条件。一位谈判者可能仅仅因为坚持己见就要求实质性让步：“价格是5000美元，就这么定了。”另一位谈判者则可能提出慷慨的报价，希望以此获得认可或友谊。无论谈判最终演变成谁更固执谁更慷慨的较量，其核心都在于双方愿意达成的协议。谈判结果是双方意志相互作用的结果——就好像谈判者生活在一个荒岛上，没有历史、没有习俗、也没有道德标准一样。

As discussed in Chapter 1, trying to reconcile differences on the basis of will has serious costs. No negotiation is likely to be efficient or amicable if you pit your will against theirs, and either you have to back down or they do. And whether you are choosing a place to eat, organizing a business, or negotiating custody of a child, you are unlikely to reach a wise agreement as judged by any objective standard if you take no such standard into account.

正如第一章所述，试图仅凭意志来调和分歧代价高昂。如果你的意志与对方的意志对抗，任何谈判都不可能高效或友好，最终要么你让步，要么对方让步。无论你是选择去哪里吃饭、组建企业，还是协商子女监护权，如果你不考虑任何客观标准，那么你都不太可能达成任何明智的协议。

If trying to settle differences of interest on the basis of will has such high costs, the solution is to negotiate on some basis independent of the will of either side—that is, on the basis of objective criteria.

如果试图通过意志来解决利益分歧的代价如此之高，那么解决办法就是在不依赖于任何一方意志的基础上进行谈判——也就是说，在客观标准的基础上进行谈判。

The case for using objective criteria

使用客观标准的理由

Suppose you have entered into a fixed-price construction contract for your house that calls for reinforced concrete foundations but fails to specify how deep they should be. The contractor suggests two feet. You think five feet is closer to the usual depth for your type of house.

假设您签订了一份房屋建造的固定价格合同，合同要求使用钢筋混凝土基础，但没有具体说明基础深度。承包商建议两英尺，而您认为五英尺更接近您这类房屋的通常基础深度。

Now suppose the contractor says: “I went along with you on steel girders for the roof. It’s your turn to go along with me on shallower foundations.” No owner in his right mind would yield. Rather than horse-trade, you would insist on deciding the issue in terms of objective safety standards. “Look, maybe I’m wrong. Maybe two feet is enough. What I want are foundations strong and deep enough to hold up the building safely. Does the government have standard specifications for these soil conditions? How deep are the foundations of other buildings in this area? What is the earthquake risk here? Where do you suggest we look for standards to resolve this question?”

现在假设承包商说：“屋顶用钢梁我同意了，现在轮到你同意我采用更浅的地基了。” 任何一个头脑清醒的业主都不会妥协。与其讨价还价，你肯定会坚持用客观的安全标准来解决这个问题。“听着，也许我错了。也许两英尺就足够了。我想要的是足够坚固和深的地基，能够安全地支撑建筑物。政府针对这种土壤条件有标准规范吗？这附近其他建筑物的地基有多深？这里的地震风险如何？你建议我们从哪里查找标准来解决这个问题？”

It is no easier to build a good contract than it is to build strong foundations. If relying on objective standards applies so clearly to a negotiation between the house owner and a contractor, why not to business deals, collective bargaining, legal settlements, and international negotiations? Why not insist that a negotiated price, for example, be based on some standard such as market value, replacement cost, depreciated book value, or competitive prices, instead of whatever the seller demands?

制定一份好的合同并不比建造坚固的地基容易。如果依靠客观标准如此明显地适用于房主和承包商之间的谈判，那么为什么不适用于商业交易、集体谈判、法律和解以及国际谈判呢？为什么不坚持要求协商价格以市场价值、重置成本、折旧账面价值或竞争价格等标准为基础，而不是以卖方的要求为准呢？

In short, the approach is to commit yourself to reaching a solution based on principle, not pressure. Concentrate on the merits of the problem, not the mettle of the parties. Be open to reason, but closed to threats.

简而言之，关键在于坚持原则，而非迫于压力寻求解决方案。关注问题的本质，而非各方的实力。要理性思考，但对威胁置若罔闻。

Principled negotiation produces wise agreements amicably and efficiently. The more you bring standards of fairness, efficiency, or scientific merit to bear on your particular problem, the more likely you are to produce a final package that is wise and fair. The more you and the other side refer to precedent and community practice, the greater your chance of benefiting from past experience. And an agreement consistent with precedent is less vulnerable to attack. If a lease contains standard terms or if a sales contract conforms to practice in the industry, there is less risk that either negotiator will feel that he was harshly treated or will later try to repudiate the agreement.

遵循原则的谈判能够友好高效地达成明智的协议。你越是运用公平、效率或科学依据来处理具体问题，就越有可能最终达成一个明智且公平的方案。你和对方越是参考先例和行业惯例，就越有可能从过往经验中获益。而且，符合先例的协议更不容易受到攻击。如果租赁合同包含标准条款，或者销售合同符合行业惯例，那么任何一方谈判者都不太可能感到自己受到了不公平的对待，或者日后试图推翻协议。

A constant battle for dominance threatens a relationship; principled negotiation protects it. It is far easier to deal with people when both of you are discussing objective standards for settling a problem instead of trying to force each other to back down.

持续不断的权力争夺会威胁彼此的关系；而有原则的协商则能保护关系。当双方都讨论解决问题的客观标准，而不是试图强迫对方让步时，处理问题就会容易得多。

Approaching agreement through discussion of objective criteria also reduces the number of commitments that each side must make and then unmake as they move toward agreement. In positional bargaining, negotiators spend much of the time defending their position and attacking the other side’s. People using objective criteria tend to use time more efficiently talking about possible standards and solutions.

通过讨论客观标准来达成协议，可以减少双方在达成协议过程中必须做出和推翻的承诺次数。在立场谈判中，谈判者往往花费大量时间来捍卫自身立场并攻击对方立场。而运用客观标准的人则能更有效地利用时间，讨论可能的标准和解决方案。

Independent standards are even more important to efficiency when more parties are involved. In such cases positional bargaining is difficult at best. It requires coalitions among parties; and the more parties who have agreed on a position, the more difficult it becomes to change that position. Similarly, if each negotiator has a constituency or has to clear a position with a higher authority, the task of adopting positions and then changing them becomes time-consuming and difficult.

当参与方更多时，独立标准对于效率的重要性就更加凸显。在这种情况下，立场谈判充其量也只能说是困难重重。它需要各方结成联盟；而达成共识的参与方越多，改变立场就越困难。同样，如果每位谈判者都有自己的支持者，或者需要向上级机构确认立场，那么制定立场以及之后更改立场的工作就会变得既耗时又费力。

An episode during the Law of the Sea negotiations illustrates the merits of using objective criteria. At one point, India, representing the Third World bloc, proposed an initial fee for companies mining in the deep seabed of $60 million per site. The United States rejected the proposal, suggesting there be no initial fee. Both sides dug in; the matter became a contest of will.

在海洋法谈判期间发生的一件事，凸显了运用客观标准的重要性。当时，代表第三世界集团的印度提议，对在深海海底采矿的公司征收每个矿址6000万美元的初始费用。美国拒绝了这一提议，认为不应征收任何初始费用。双方各执己见，最终演变成一场意志力的较量。

Then someone discovered that the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) had developed a model for the economics of deep-seabed mining. This model, gradually accepted by the parties as objective, provided a way of evaluating the impact of any fee proposal on the economics of mining. When the Indian representative asked about the effect of his proposal, he was shown how the tremendous fee he proposed—payable five years before the mine would generate any revenue—would make it virtually impossible for a company to mine. Impressed, he announced that he would reconsider his position. On the other side, the MIT model helped educate the American representatives, whose information on the subject had been mostly limited to that provided by the mining companies. The model indicated that some initial fee was economically feasible. As a result, the United States also changed its position.

后来有人发现，麻省理工学院（MIT）开发了一种深海采矿经济模型。该模型逐渐被各方接受，并被视为客观有效，它提供了一种评估任何收费方案对采矿经济影响的方法。当印度代表询问其方案的影响时，有人向他展示了他提出的巨额费用——需要在矿山产生任何收益的五年前支付——实际上会使任何公司都无法进行开采。他深受触动，并表示将重新考虑自己的立场。另一方面，MIT的模型也帮助美国代表了解了相关情况，此前他们对这一问题的了解主要局限于矿业公司提供的信息。该模型表明，收取一定的初始费用在经济上是可行的。因此，美国也改变了立场。

No one backed down; no one appeared weak—just reasonable. After a lengthy negotiation, the parties reached a tentative agreement that was mutually satisfactory.

谁也不让步，谁也不示弱——大家都表现得通情达理。经过长时间的谈判，双方最终达成了一项彼此都满意的初步协议。

The MIT model increased the chance of agreement and decreased costly posturing. It led to a better solution, one that would both attract companies to do mining and generate considerable revenue for the nations of the world. The existence of an objective model able to forecast the consequences of any proposal helped convince the parties that the tentative agreement they reached was fair. This in turn strengthened relationships among the negotiators and made it more likely an agreement would endure. [2]

麻省理工学院模型提高了达成协议的可能性，减少了代价高昂的对抗。它促成了一个更优的解决方案，既能吸引企业从事采矿业，又能为世界各国创造可观的收入。客观模型的存在能够预测任何提案的后果，这有助于各方相信他们达成的初步协议是公平的。这反过来又加强了谈判者之间的关系，并使协议更有可能持久有效。[2]

Developing objective criteria

制定客观标准

Carrying on a principled negotiation involves two questions: How do you develop objective criteria, and how do you use them in negotiating?

进行有原则的谈判涉及两个问题：如何制定客观标准，以及如何在谈判中使用这些标准？

Whatever method of negotiation you use, you will do better if you prepare in advance. This certainly holds true of principled negotiation. So develop some alternative standards beforehand and think through their application to your case.

无论你采用何种谈判方法，提前做好准备都会更有利。这一点在原则性谈判中尤为重要。因此，请事先制定一些备选标准，并仔细思考如何将其应用于你的具体案例。

Fair standards. You will usually find more than one objective criterion available as a basis for agreement. Suppose, for example, your car is demolished and you file a claim with an insurance company. In your discussion with the adjuster, you might take into account such measures of the car’s value as (1) the original cost of the car less depreciation; (2) what the car could have been sold for; (3) the standard “blue book” value for a car of that year and model; (4) what it would cost to replace that car with a comparable one; and (5) what a court might award as the value of the car.

公平标准。通常情况下，你会发现有不止一个客观标准可以作为达成共识的基础。例如，假设你的车被撞毁，你向保险公司提出索赔。在与理赔员讨论时，你可能会考虑以下几个衡量车辆价值的因素：（1）车辆的原始价格减去折旧；（2）车辆原本可以卖多少钱；（3）同年份同型号车辆的标准“蓝皮书”估价；（4）购买一辆同等车型所需的费用；以及（5）法院可能判决的车辆价值。

In other cases, depending on the issue, you may wish to propose that an agreement be based upon:

在其他情况下，根据具体问题，您可能希望提议协议基于以下原则：

Market value

市场价值

What a court would decide

法院会如何裁决

Precedent

先例

Moral standards

道德标准

Scientific judgment

科学判断

Equal treatment

平等待遇

Professional standards

专业标准

Tradition

传统

Efficiency

效率

Reciprocity

互惠

Costs

成本

Etc.

ETC。

At a minimum, objective criteria need to be independent of each side’s will. Ideally, to assure a wise agreement, objective criteria should be not only independent of will but also both legitimate and practical. In a boundary dispute, for example, you may find it easier to agree on a physically salient feature such as a river than on a line three yards to the east of the riverbank.

至少，客观标准必须独立于双方的意愿。理想情况下，为了确保达成明智的协议，客观标准不仅应独立于意愿，还应兼具合法性和实用性。例如，在边界纠纷中，您可能会发现，就河流等显著的地理特征达成一致，比就河岸东侧三码处的一条线达成一致更容易。

Objective criteria should apply, at least in theory, to both sides. You can thus use the test of reciprocal application to tell you whether a proposed criterion is fair and independent of either party’s will. If a real estate agency selling you a house offers a standard form contract, you would be wise to ask if that is the same standard form they use when they buy a house. In the international arena, the principle of self-determination is notorious for the number of peoples who insist on it as a fundamental right but deny its applicability to those on the other side. Consider the Middle East, Kashmir, or Cyprus as just three examples.

客观标准至少在理论上应当适用于双方。因此，你可以运用互惠适用原则来判断一项拟议标准是否公平且独立于任何一方的意愿。如果一家房地产中介公司向你出售房屋时提供了一份标准格式合同，你最好询问一下，他们自己买房时是否也使用同样的标准格式合同。在国际舞台上，自决原则因许多民族坚持将其视为一项基本权利，却否认其适用于对方而臭名昭著。中东、克什米尔和塞浦路斯便是三个例证。

Fair procedures. To produce an outcome independent of will, you can use either fair standards for the substantive question or fair procedures for resolving the conflicting interests. Consider, for example, the age-old way to divide a piece of cake between two children: one cuts and the other chooses. Neither can complain about an unfair division.

公平的程序。为了确保结果不受意志的影响，你可以对实质性问题采用公平的标准，也可以对冲突的利益采用公平的程序来解决。例如，想想过去分蛋糕给两个孩子的方法：一个孩子切蛋糕，另一个孩子挑选。这样，谁也不会抱怨分得不公平。

This simple procedure was used in the Law of the Sea negotiations, one of the most complex negotiations ever undertaken. At one point, the issue of how to allocate mining sites in the deep seabed deadlocked the negotiation. Under the terms of the draft agreement, half the sites were to be mined by private companies, the other half by the Enterprise, a mining organization to be owned by the United Nations. Since the private mining companies from the rich nations had the technology and the expertise to choose the best sites, the poorer nations feared the less knowledgeable Enterprise would receive a bad bargain.

这一简易程序曾用于《海洋法公约》谈判，而《海洋法公约》是历史上最复杂的谈判之一。谈判一度陷入僵局，焦点在于如何分配深海海底的采矿区。根据协议草案，一半的采矿区将由私营公司开采，另一半则由联合国下属的采矿组织“企业”开采。由于富裕国家的私营矿业公司拥有选择最佳采矿区的技术和专业知识，较贫穷的国家担心，经验不足的“企业”会吃亏。

The solution devised was to agree that a private company seeking to mine the seabed would present the Enterprise with two proposed mining sites. The Enterprise would pick one site for itself and grant the company a license to mine the other. Since the company would not know which site it would get, it would have an incentive to make both sites as promising as possible. This simple procedure thus harnessed the company’s superior expertise for mutual gain.

最终的解决方案是：一家有意开采海底资源的私营公司向企业提交两个拟建的矿址。企业从中选择一个矿址，并授予该公司另一个矿址的开采许可证。由于该公司事先并不知道会获得哪个矿址，因此它有动力尽可能地提高两个矿址的开采潜力。这一简单的流程便能充分利用该公司的专业技术，实现互利共赢。

A variation on the procedure of “one cuts, the other chooses” is for the parties to negotiate what they think is a fair arrangement before they go on to decide their respective roles in it. In a divorce negotiation, for example, before deciding which parent will get custody of the children, the parents might agree on the visiting rights (and responsibilities) of the other parent. This gives both an incentive to agree on visitation rights each will think fair.

“一人裁，一人选”的协商程序的一种变体是，双方先协商出一个他们认为公平的安排，然后再决定各自在其中的角色。例如，在离婚谈判中，在决定子女监护权归属之前，父母可以先就另一方的探视权（和责任）达成一致。这促使双方都积极协商出双方都认为公平的探视权。

As you consider procedural solutions, look at other basic means of settling differences: taking turns, drawing lots, letting someone else decide, and so on.

在考虑程序性解决方案时，不妨看看其他解决分歧的基本方法：轮流、抽签、让别人做决定等等。

Frequently, taking turns presents the best way for heirs to divide a large number of heirlooms left to them collectively. Afterwards, they can do some trading if they want. Or they can make the selection tentative so they see how it comes out before committing themselves to accept it. Drawing lots, flipping a coin, and other forms of chance have an inherent fairness. The results may be unequal, but each side had an equal opportunity.

通常情况下，轮流分配是继承人共同分割大量传家宝的最佳方式。之后，他们可以根据意愿进行一些交换。或者，他们可以先进行初步选择，看看结果如何，然后再决定是否接受。抽签、抛硬币和其他形式的随机分配方式都具有内在的公平性。结果可能并不完全相等，但每一方都有平等的机会。

Letting someone else play a key role in a joint decision is a well-established procedure with almost infinite variations. The parties can agree to submit a particular question to an expert for advice or decision. They can ask a mediator to help them reach a decision. Or they can submit the matter to an arbitrator for an authoritative and binding decision.

让其他人参与共同决策是一种成熟的程序，其形式几乎无穷无尽。各方可以约定将特定问题提交专家咨询或裁决；可以请求调解员协助达成决定；也可以将事项提交仲裁员作出权威且具有约束力的裁决。

Professional baseball, for example, uses “last-best-offer arbitration” to settle player salary disputes. The arbitrator must choose between the last offer made by one side and the last offer made by the other. The theory is that this procedure puts pressure on the parties to make their proposals more reasonable. In baseball, and in states where this form of arbitration is compulsory for certain public employee disputes, it does seem to produce more settlements than in comparable circumstances where there is a commitment to conventional arbitration; those parties who don’t settle, however, sometimes give the arbitrator an unpleasant choice between two extreme offers.

例如，职业棒球采用“最后最佳报价仲裁”来解决球员薪资纠纷。仲裁员必须在双方提出的最后报价中做出选择。理论上，这种程序会迫使双方提出更合理的报价。在棒球界，以及某些州强制要求对特定公职人员纠纷采用这种仲裁方式，这种仲裁方式似乎比采用传统仲裁的类似情况更容易达成和解；然而，那些未能达成和解的当事人有时会让仲裁员在两个极端报价中做出艰难的选择。

Negotiating with objective criteria

以客观标准进行谈判

Having identified some objective criteria and procedures, how do you go about discussing them with the other side?

确定了一些客观标准和程序之后，你该如何与对方进行讨论呢？

There are three basic points to remember:

需要记住三点基本要点：

  1. Frame each issue as a joint search for objective criteria.
    将每个问题都视为共同寻求客观标准的过程。
  2. Reason and be open to reason as to which standards are most appropriate and how they should be applied.
    要理性思考，并乐于接受合理的解释，以确定哪些标准最合适以及如何应用这些标准。
  3. Never yield to pressure, only to principle.
    永远不要屈服于压力，只坚守原则。

In short, focus on objective criteria firmly but flexibly.

简而言之，要坚定而灵活地关注客观标准。

Frame each issue as a joint search for objective criteria. If you are negotiating to buy a house, you might start off by saying: “Look, you want a high price and I want a low one. Let’s figure out what a fair price would be. What objective standards might be most relevant?” You and the other side may have conflicting interests, but the two of you now have a shared goal: to determine a fair price. You might begin by suggesting one or more criteria yourself—the cost of the house adjusted for depreciation and inflation, recent sale prices of similar houses in the neighborhood, or an independent appraisal—and then invite the seller’s suggestions.

将每个问题都视为共同寻找客观标准的过程。如果你正在协商买房，你可以这样开头：“你看，你想要高价，我想要低价。我们一起来探讨一下，什么样的价格才算合理。哪些客观标准最相关呢？”你和对方的利益可能存在冲突，但你们现在有了一个共同的目标：确定一个合理的价格。你可以先提出一个或多个标准——例如，根据折旧和通货膨胀调整后的房价、附近类似房屋的近期成交价，或者一份独立的评估报告——然后再邀请卖方提出他们的建议。

Ask “What’s your theory?” If the seller starts by giving you a position, such as “The price is $255,000,” ask for the theory behind that price: “How did you arrive at that figure?” Treat the problem as though the seller too is looking for a fair price based on objective criteria.

问“你的想法是什么？”如果卖家一开始就报出一个价格，比如“价格是25.5万美元”，那就追问这个价格背后的逻辑：“你是怎么得出这个数字的？”要像卖家一样，基于客观标准来寻找一个公平的价格。

Agree first on principles. Before even considering possible terms, you may want to agree on the standard or standards to apply.

首先要就原则达成一致。在考虑具体条款之前，你们可能需要先就适用的标准达成一致。

Each standard the other side proposes becomes a lever you can then use to persuade them. Your case will have more impact if it is presented in terms of their criteria, and they will find it difficult to resist applying their criteria to the problem. “You say Mr. Jones sold the house next door for $260,000. Your theory is that this house should be sold for what comparable houses in the neighborhood are going for, am I right? In that case, let’s look at what the house on the corner of Ellsworth and Oxford and the one at Broadway and Dana were sold for.” What makes conceding particularly difficult is having to accept someone else’s proposal. If they suggested the standard, their deferring to it is not an act of weakness but an act of strength, of carrying out their word.

对方提出的每一项标准都成了你用来说服他们的杠杆。如果你的论点以他们的标准为依据，就会更有说服力，他们也很难抗拒将这些标准应用于这个问题。“你说琼斯先生把隔壁的房子卖了26万美元。你的理论是，这栋房子也应该以附近类似房屋的售价出售，对吗？如果是这样，那我们就来看看埃尔斯沃思街和牛津街拐角处的房子，以及百老汇大街和达纳街拐角处的房子分别卖了多少钱。” 让步之所以特别困难，是因为你必须接受别人的提议。如果标准是他们提出的，那么他们接受它并非软弱的表现，而是强硬的表现，是信守承诺的表现。

Reason and be open to reason. What makes the negotiation a joint search is that, however much you may have prepared various objective criteria, you come to the table with an open mind. In most negotiations, people use precedent and other objective standards simply as arguments in support of a position. A police union might, for example, insist upon a raise of a certain amount and then justify their position with arguments about what police in other cities make. This use of standards usually only digs people even deeper into their position.

理性思考，并保持开放的心态去接受理性。谈判之所以能成为共同探索，就在于无论你事先准备了多少客观标准，都要以开放的心态参与其中。在大多数谈判中，人们仅仅将先例和其他客观标准作为支持自身立场的论据。例如，警察工会可能会坚持要求加薪一定数额，然后用其他城市警察的薪资水平来佐证自己的立场。这种对标准的滥用通常只会让人们更加固执己见。

Going one step further, some people begin by announcing that their position is an issue of principle and refuse even to consider the other side’s case. “It’s a matter of principle” becomes a battle cry in a holy war over ideology. Practical differences escalate into principled ones, further locking in the negotiators rather than freeing them.

更进一步，有些人一开始就宣称自己的立场是原则问题，甚至拒绝考虑对方的论点。“这是原则问题”成了意识形态圣战中的战斗口号。实际分歧升级为原则性分歧，这非但没有解放谈判者，反而让他们更加进退维谷。

This is emphatically not what is meant by principled negotiation. Insisting that an agreement be based on objective criteria does not mean insisting that it be based solely on the criterion you advance. One standard of legitimacy does not preclude the existence of others. What the other side believes to be fair may not be what you believe to be fair. You should behave like a judge; although you may be predisposed to one side (in this case, your own), you should be willing to respond to reasons for applying another standard or for applying a standard differently. When each party is advancing a different standard, look for an objective basis for deciding between them, such as which standard has been used by the parties in the past or which standard is more widely applied. Just as the substantive issue itself should not be settled on the basis of will, neither should the question of which standard applies.

这绝非原则性谈判的真正含义。坚持协议必须基于客观标准，并不意味着坚持协议只能基于你提出的标准。一种合法性标准并不排除其他标准的存在。对方认为公平的，可能与你认为公平的并不相同。你应该像法官一样行事；即使你可能倾向于某一方（在本例中是你自己），你也应该愿意回应对方提出的适用其他标准或以不同方式适用同一标准的理由。当双方提出不同的标准时，你应该寻找客观依据来做出选择，例如双方过去使用过哪种标准，或者哪种标准应用更为广泛。正如实质性问题本身不应基于意愿来解决一样，适用哪种标准的问题也不应如此。

In a given case, there may be two standards (such as market value and depreciated cost) that produce different results but that both parties agree seem equally legitimate. In that case, splitting the difference or otherwise compromising between the results suggested by the two objective standards is perfectly legitimate. The outcome is still independent of the will of the parties.

在特定情况下，可能存在两种标准（例如市场价值和折旧成本），它们得出的结果不同，但双方都认为这两种标准同样合理。在这种情况下，取其一半或以其他方式在两种客观标准得出的结果之间做出妥协是完全合理的。最终结果仍然独立于当事人的意愿。

If, however, after a thorough discussion of the merits of an issue you still cannot accept their proposed criteria as the most appropriate, you might suggest putting them to a test. Agree on someone you both regard as fair and give him or her a list of the proposed criteria. Ask the person to decide which are the fairest or most appropriate for your situation. Since objective criteria are supposed to be legitimate and because legitimacy implies acceptance by a great many people, this is a fair thing to ask. You are not asking the third party to settle your substantive dispute—just to give you advice on what standard to use in settling it.

然而，如果经过充分讨论后，您仍然无法接受他们提出的标准，您可以建议对这些标准进行检验。双方共同选定一位您认为公正的人，并将这些标准清单交给他/她。请他/她判断哪些标准最公平或最适合您的情况。由于客观标准理应具有合法性，而合法性意味着得到大多数人的认可，因此提出这样的要求是合理的。您并非要求第三方解决您的实质性争议，而只是请他/她就解决争议时应采用的标准提供建议。

The difference between seeking agreement on the appropriate principles for deciding a matter and using principles simply as arguments to support positions is sometimes subtle, but always significant. A principled negotiator is open to reasoned persuasion on the merits; a positional bargainer is not. It is the combination of openness to reason with insistence on a solution based on objective criteria that makes principled negotiation so persuasive and so effective at getting the other side to play.

寻求就决策的适当原则达成一致，与仅仅将原则作为支持自身立场的论据，二者之间的区别有时很微妙，但始终至关重要。有原则的谈判者愿意接受基于事实的理性劝说；而立场型谈判者则不然。正是这种对理性开放的态度与坚持基于客观标准寻求解决方案的理念相结合，使得有原则的谈判如此具有说服力，如此有效地促使对方参与谈判。

Never yield to pressure. Consider once again the example of negotiating with the contractor. What if he offers to hire your brother-in-law on the condition that you give in on the depth of the foundations? You would probably answer, “A job for my brother-in-law has nothing to do with whether the house will be safely supported on a foundation of that depth.” What if the contractor then threatens to charge you a higher price? You would answer the same way: “We’ll settle that question on the merits too. Let’s see what other contractors charge for this kind of work,” or “Bring me your cost figures and we’ll work out a fair profit margin.” If the contractor replies, “Come on, you trust me, don’t you?” you would respond: “Trust is an entirely separate matter.
